Run-off from farms cause of high bacteria level in river
Not farms, septic tanks. It's human feces that is causing the bulk of it.

Fromt the article:

“And it's about 80 percent cattle. Agriculture is really booming in Mid-Michigan,” Cheatham said. “We're putting more and more animals on the land than ever before, and that manure has to go somewhere. It's going in our rivers.”

So you didn't even bother to read it, I see.

This is a big problem, you simply wouldn't believe how much shit comes out of cattle farms. A single dairy cow produces 22.5 tons of manure per year (S). If this is allowed to mix with rain water and run off it will poison a river very easy. Farms need major redesign to be able to handle this much concentrated refuse.

The best way is to collect it in digesters and produce biogas out of it. There is enough energy in that waste to allow a farm to produce all its heating + electricity + agricultural fuel from animal refuse. Unfortunately this is an involved chemical process and like all processes it requires constant monitoring and engineering expertise. This is why farmers are unlikely to adopt it and reach viable efficiencies.

The second best way is to compost it and turn it into fertilizer. The same energy gets used by the soil microorganisms and fungi which digest the carbohydrates for energy and make the minerals available for plants. This is close to the natural process but much more concentrated. It is somewhat risky because spread of disease is easy and water contamination is still possible in some soil types.

The worst way is to allow it to mix with rain water and run off into the sewers or into rivers. Massive contamination and spread of disease is guaranteed.
